prediction.named_residual: receiver-shape axis discriminability — claim that smooth-S-curve and step-function receivers produce statistically distinguishable coupling-slope distributions. peer-checks the framing that smooth_receiver_coupling_alarm_v1 (PR #42) + cajal/miles PR #35 / #37 convergence rest on.
prediction.alarm_semantics: PASS = receiver-shape axis is mechanically discriminative (mean(smooth_slopes) − mean(step_slopes) ≥ 0.15 AND ≥75% of smooth slopes exceed the step-class median); FAIL = distributions overlap, framing not supported by the substrate.

kill_condition.rule: PASS iff mean(smooth_slopes) − mean(step_slopes) ≥ 0.15 AND ≥75% of smooth pair slopes exceed median(step_slopes); FAIL otherwise. The voice treats the receiver-shape axis as falsified if either criterion does not hold.
kill_condition.rationale: If the receiver-shape distinction is real, smooth-S-curve pairs should concentrate at high slope values (over-correlation kill region) while step-function pairs should not. Requiring BOTH a mean separation AND a quantile-level dominance check guards against the distributions having similar means but heavy overlap, or being separated by outliers. If either criterion fails, the receiver-shape framing is a name without mechanical discriminator and the PR #42 alarm is operating on an over-fit axis.

verdict.rationale: receiver-shape axis NOT mechanically discriminative; failed: mean_separation -0.0551 < 0.15; smooth_above_step_median_frac 25.00% < 75%. PR #42's framing is over-fit to the small observed-pair set — the receiver-shape claim needs re-description or the synthetic substrate is missing the distinguishing dynamic.
